subject: Runtime-led pilot: flex credits, batching & quant plan
messages:
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@cortexworks.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: pilot structure for Optimize toolkit (batching/cache/quant)

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the demo last week. CortexWorks is keen to run a short pilot of Redwood's Optimize toolkit to test cost savings and latency for our vector search ranking pipeline. A few details to help scope:
- Workload: ~5M inference requests/day, median prompt length ~180 tokens, 95p sequence ~520 tokens.
- Access pattern: heavy prefix reuse (same system prompts + user history), and many short reranking calls following a candidate generation step.
- Goal: reduce token costs ~30% while keeping end-to-end 95p latency under 250ms for reranking calls.

Questions:
1) What pilot packaging do you recommend (credits vs committed tier) for a 90-day evaluation?
2) Can you outline batching/caching knobs we should try first and any ops tradeoffs?
3) We're exploring int8 quantization but worried about rare hallucination regressions — can Redwood provide guidance or a safe rollback approach?

Attached is a quick CSV with hourly QPS for the last two weeks. Happy to set a sync if useful.

Best,
Maria
Head of Platform, CortexWorks

[attachment: workload-patterns.csv]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@cortexworks.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: pilot structure for Optimize toolkit (batching/cache/quant)

Hi Maria —

Appreciate the context and the CSV — that's helpful. Short answers up front, then a suggested pilot construct.

1) Pilot packaging: for a 90-day evaluation we typically do a flexible-credit pilot (non-binding credit pool) sized to cover expected egress + inference tokens. For your 5M requests/day profile I recommend a 600k credit pool (~30% buffer); we convert credits to effective per-token rates in the SOW so there are no surprise overruns. If you prefer a committed short-term tier we can convert credits into a short-term reserve with a simple reconciliation.

2) Batching/caching knobs: start with these three:
   - Continuous micro-batching: set target batch window 10–25ms for rerank calls to preserve latency while gaining batching savings.
   - Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix cache for system prompt + user history blocks; this is where you'll see the biggest win given your reuse patterns. We recommend a TTL of 15 minutes for session affinity and a warmup plan to prime hot keys.
   - Adaptive batch sizing: let the runtime grow batches up to 256 tokens for the generation stage, but cap it for the rerank path to avoid latency tail risk.

Ops tradeoffs: aggressive batching increases throughput but can add 10–40ms to P99 if windows are too large. Cache priming reduces cold-starts but requires a cache eviction policy tuned to your session churn. We'll provide a dashboard tile that shows per-route batching efficiency and cache hit rate.

3) Quantization guidance: int8 provides ~1.6–2.2x token-cost improvement on our test models. For CortexWorks' reranking workload I suggest starting with mixed-profile quantization: run int8 for non-critical internal rerank models and float16 for top-N finalizers. We'll run A/B evals on your prompt set to measure ngram recall and hallucination deltas. Rollback plan: we've got automatic fallback to the float16 variant per request, plus canary routing (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with automated quality gates.

Next steps I propose:
- I attach a brief SOW draft with a credit conversion table and pilot milestones (see pilot-sow-v1.pdf).
- Connor and Soojin can pick the initial runtime knobs; Connor will run a short load test, Soojin will set up the eval harness.
- If that sounds good, can we lock a kickoff for Wed or Thu this week?

Connor / Soojin: can you confirm availability and whether we need an infra walkthrough or temporary VPC access?

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya — this is very clear. A couple of follow-ups before we kickoff:

- Credit conversion: can you give a worked example in the SOW of how 600k credits map to per-token rates for generation vs embeddings vs reranking calls? The team needs that to model spend.
- SLA / logs: during the pilot we need access logs for compliance (no PII in logs). Is it possible to exclude sensitive fields from exported traces?
- Quant A/B: we'd like Redwood to run the A/B evals on our prompt set and publish a short quality report (delta on top-K recall and hallucination indicators) before moving beyond canary.

We're good for a Wednesday kickoff — available 10:00–11:30 PT. I'll route the internal CS folks to join the call.

Maria

Subject: Re: Quick ask: pilot structure for Optimize toolkit (batching/cache/quant)

Maria —

Great; summary and agreed actions below so we have a single source-of-truth before the Wednesday kickoff.

Summary of pilot (agreed):
- 90-day flexible-credit pilot sized at 600k credits (CW-2028-OPT-42). Credits are non-binding for evaluation; unused credits during pilot can be credited toward conversion if you decide on committed capacity.
- Credit conversion example (in SOW): 1 credit = $0.015 effective unit. Example mapping (illustrative): generation token = 0.007 credits/token, embedding unit = 0.12 credits/1000 vectors, rerank call (avg 220 tokens input + 40 tokens output) = ~3.1 credits per call. SOW contains exact conversion table and reconciliation flow.
- Technical knobs for first 30 days: micro-batch window 15ms for rerank route, KV prefix caching with 15-minute TTL and proactive priming for top-500 sessions, adaptive batch ceiling 256 tokens for generation route.
- Quant strategy: start with mixed-profile rollout: int8 on non-final rerank variant, float16 on finalizer. Redwood will run A/B evals on your provided prompt set and publish a quality delta report (top-K recall, hallucination rate proxies). Canary gating: 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated rollback on quality regressions.
- Observability & logs: we can provide redacted access logs for the pilot (strip PII/PII-like fields). We will surface per-route cost and hit-rate dashboards and a daily CSV export to your secure bucket.

Action items and owners:
- Priya: finalize SOW (I will add the worked credit conversion examples and the HubSpot deal link).
- Connor: confirm load-test VM and provide temporary read-only VPC endpoint by EOD Mon.
- Soojin: create eval harness and plan (A/B metrics and the gating thresholds).
- Maria: confirm Wednesday 10:30 PT for kickoff and share any additional personas to include on the invite.

Kickoff: Wed, 24 May 2028 @ 10:30 PT — I'll send a calendar invite with agenda and owners.

Thanks everyone — excited to get this running.

— Priya
